items.title: fix(flash next cuda): a lone stream keeps its graphs once kept prompt ends fill every slot (#317)
items.body:
Fixes #317, as @Arminova diagnosed it there: on 0.6.4 and 0.6.5, once `--parallel N` has kept a prompt end in every slot, each new lone request moves the graphs to its own slot and captures its decode windows again.

Four commits on v0.6.4 (they apply to v0.6.5 unchanged; `multi.py` and `multi_solo.py` are the same in both). Each stands on its own:
1. **A fresh prompt takes the idle graph slot.** When the graph slot is idle and holds kept ends, they move to a spare with 0.6.4's `_relocate_kept` (the slot the prompt was given, when no other is free), and the prompt decodes in the graph slot, whose rows and graphs stay. No kept end is evicted. Two ranks keep their planned path.
2. **Each slot keeps the graphs captured over it until it is resized.** Where the graphs still move to a stream's own slot (a resumed turn whose kept end lives elsewhere, with no spare), the slot they leave keeps its set, and a slot that held one takes it back. `_state_changed` drops a slot's set before any resize, including `_relocate_kept`'s spare.
3. **Tests**, which fail on 0.6.4 and pass with the commits:
   - `tests/cuda/test_flashnext_lone_slot.py`: eight different prompts on 5 slots capture exactly what 1 slot does, request by request, with the same tokens as the single-sequence engine (bf16 and int8). A warmed graph slot captures nothing for new prompts on a full pool. Two conversations taking turns make no new graph set after each one's slot has held the graphs once. The no-room fallback (commit 4).
   - `tests/test_flashnext_lone_slot.py`: the same slot logic on the host with stand-in slots, no GPU.
4. **Separable:** when the graph slot can't grow to a lone stream's cache (no room for the copy's peak), `_move_to_solo` raised "the lone stream's graph slot cannot hold its existing cache" and the round failed. On one GPU the graphs now go to the stream's slot instead, as they already do when a kept end holds the graph slot. Two ranks keep the error. Happy to split this into its own PR.

Arminova's proposed fix (evict the oldest kept end) fails 0.6.4's `test_packed_passes_keep_each_prompt_one_token_early`, as we noted on #317. This version evicts nothing.

One thing it doesn't change: `_relocate_kept` (and commit 1, which calls it) resizes the spare to the graph slot's whole capacity and copies all of it. A graph slot that grew with one long conversation therefore grows every spare that takes its kept ends. We run a fix that copies only the kept rows. It's a separate change.

**Environment.**
- One DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), driver 580.178.04, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, CUDA 13.0.
- `turboderp/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-exl3` `4.05bpw_h6_ng6` at revision `55a732e`, with its stock MTP head. No local patches and no `TF_*` variables in any arm.
- Builds: stock v0.6.4 (`6ea5ade`) against v0.6.4 plus this PR (`227b97e`, `32f3af1`, `292e38d`, `65bf4dd`). Outside the tests, only `multi.py` and `multi_solo.py` change.
- Server: `tensorfold serve <ckpt> --parallel 5 --context 262144 --kv-dtype int8`, plus `--parallel 1` as the control. That is @Arminova's command without `--ple-on-ssd`, which 0.6.4 refuses for an EXL3 pack, and without `--thinking`. Each arm booted with the n-gram file's page cache dropped.
- Counting: as in @Arminova's run, a wrapper counts `Graphs()` sets, `Graphs._capture`, `_state_changed` on the graph slot and `_move_to_solo`. It loads before `tensorfold serve` and leaves the engine unchanged. Every arm ran through it.
- Requests: @Arminova's shape, eight different short prompts one after another, 128 tokens, greedy, thinking off, `ignore_eos`. Then the same eight again (pass 2), which resumes the kept prompt ends that are still there.

**Exactness.**
- Per build, `--parallel 5` against `--parallel 1`: the same `token_sha` and the same rounds, request by request. Stock: 16/16 in both stock arms. With the fix: 16/16 in both fix arms.
- Across builds, all 96 eight-prompt requests (6 arms, 2 passes of 8) carry the same `token_sha`: yes.
- `bench_concurrent.py --alone --serial` (levels 1, 2 and 4, 128 tokens, 2 reps, `--parallel 5`):
  - with the fix: concurrent against alone 56 / 0 / 0 equal / unequal / failed; alone against `"draft": false` 30 / 0 / 0;
  - stock: 56 / 0 / 0 and 30 / 0 / 0.

**Decode speed.** `--parallel 5`, decode seconds per request (first token to last) and the graphs captured in that request. Pass 1 is the run in alternated order: stock, fix, fix, stock.

| request | stock `--parallel 1` | stock `--parallel 5` | captured | fix `--parallel 5` | captured | fix `--parallel 1` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1-5 | 10.16 | 10.29 | 0 | 10.24 | 0 | 10.29 |
| 6 | 2.00 | 3.98 | 18 | 2.03 | 0 | 1.99 |
| 7 | 1.97 | 3.93 | 18 | 2.00 | 0 | 1.96 |
| 8 | 2.03 | 4.04 | 19 | 2.07 | 0 | 2.04 |

- Requests 6-8 in total, `--parallel 5`: stock 11.95 and 11.88 s (first and second stock arm), fix 6.09 and 5.99 s. `--parallel 1`: 6.00 s stock, 5.99 s fix.
- Graph sets made after startup, pass 1: stock 3, fix 0 (each arm). Graph slot moves: stock 3, fix 0 (the fix moves the slot's kept end instead, 7 times).
- Pass 2 (the same eight prompts again; requests whose kept end survived resume it): captures stock 143 and 143, fix 0 and 0; graph slot moves stock 8, fix 0. Decode for all eight: stock 31.64 and 30.43 s, fix 16.33 s, `--parallel 1` 16.04 s (stock) and 16.44 s (fix).
- `bench_openai.py` (default: 64 tokens, T 1 and T 0, 5 reps), median tok/s, in order stock / fix / fix / stock:
  - fibonacci T 1: 61.0 / 73.0 / 73.8 / 64.6
  - chat T 1: 48.6 / 51.5 / 52.9 / 49.9
  - fibonacci T 0: 78.7 / 78.4 / 79.9 / 80.2
  - chat T 0: 54.0 / 53.5 / 54.8 / 54.9

**Prompt speed.** `prefill_cold.py`, median TTFT, stock / fix, one run each, not alternated: 2K 3.03 / 3.12 s, 8K 12.43 / 12.38 s, 16K 25.17 / 24.93 s, 32K 50.21 / 50.30 s, 64K 99.21 / 100.80 s. To fit the window we ran a trimmed set: three prompts at 2K and 8K, one each at 16K, 32K and 64K. The change selects slots and graph sets. It doesn't touch prefill.

**Tests.** On GB10:
- New `tests/cuda/test_flashnext_lone_slot.py`: 6 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped with the fix. On stock 0.6.4 the same file gives 0 / 6 / 0. It fails from the sixth prompt, which is @Arminova's request 6. It covers:
  - eight different prompts on 5 slots capture exactly what 1 slot does, request by request, with the same tokens (bf16 and int8);
  - a warmed graph slot captures nothing for new prompts on a full pool;
  - two conversations taking turns make no new graph set after each one's slot has held the graphs once;
  - the no-room fallback.
- New `tests/test_flashnext_lone_slot.py` (host, stand-in slots, no GPU): 4 passed with the fix, 4 failed on stock.
- `tests/cuda/test_flashnext_multi.py` and `test_flashnext_graph_capacity.py` with the fix: 30 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped.

**About the "3 extra captures" in our #317 comment.** The test counted from the start of turn 1. That turn is the first time the first conversation's own slot takes the graphs, so it captures its set once: 3 graphs on the synthetic model, which is all the graph slot had captured over 10 requests. That was the whole difference (`6 == 3`). We traced the slot logic on the CPU, with stand-in slots and a stand-in `Graphs`:
- After that first capture, no turn makes a new set through 12 turns, for 3 to 5 slots and `keep` 4 or 8.
- On stock 0.6.4 the same trace makes a new set on every request once the pool is full.
- The CUDA test above therefore counts from turn 2.

**What we did not run.**
- The MLX 4-bit checkpoint and `--ple-on-ssd` (EXL3 only here). Metal.
- Two ranks. The fix acts on one GPU only, and two ranks keep 0.6.4's planned path.
- The memory the kept graph sets take: we only recorded MemAvailable, lowest 14.3 GiB with the fix and 14.4 GiB on stock. Each set has its own graph pool, so with `--parallel N` at most N sets are kept.
- The full `prefill_cold` set: 1 rep, not 3, at 16K, 32K and 64K.
- Your 256- and 1,024-token lengths.
- The full host suite with these commits. We ran the new host file above. Outside the tests, the commits change only `multi.py` and `multi_solo.py`, which the host suite does not import without CUDA.

Thanks to @Arminova for the diagnosis and the eight-prompt protocol.

Written with AI assistance (Claude Code).

items.title: Flash Next on CUDA: copy drafts where a reply repeats earlier text
items.body:
## What

Copy drafts for Flash Next on CUDA. When a stream's last 8 tokens occur earlier in its prompt or reply, the round drafts that text's continuation whole, up to the depth, instead of asking the MTP head. The verify step is unchanged, so every reply equals one-token decoding. Nemotron already does this (`nemotron_h/cuda/decode.py: CopyIndex`); this is the same index, in its own module for the family, wired into the four places Flash Next drafts: the serial MTP loop (`decode.py: mtp_decode`), the shared rounds (`multi.py: _draft_all`), the lone stream's graph slot (`multi_solo.py: _solo_round`) and the first drafts after a prompt (`multi_fill.py: _joined`). The kept rows still go into the MTP cache, so the head resumes cleanly on the next round that needs it.

Two ranks: both hold the same tokens (sampling is gathered), so both build the same index and propose the same chain, and the round plan digest (`multi_tp.shape`) already covers each stream's drafts. In the shared rounds the first chain level's picks still cover every absorbed stream, because the two-rank gather reads them in order; a copying stream's pick is dropped and it joins no later level.

On by default with MTP drafts; `TENSORFOLD_COPY_DRAFTS=0` turns it off. Off without MTP drafts and for grammar-constrained replies. A 250k-token prompt indexes in 0.12 s at admission; a chain lookup is microseconds.

I read #286: the Python engine is frozen and new work goes to the Zig engine. Flash Next is not on CUDA there yet, so this is offered as the reference implementation and the measurements for when it is; rewrite it however fits. #444 describes a prompt-lookup drafter for this family on EXL3 with the same conclusion (copy-heavy replies gain, fresh text does not); this one reuses Nemotron's index and runs on two ranks.

## Receipt

**Environment.** TensorFold `cb2ebf0` (v0.6.6 = `main`) plus this branch, inside `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3` (PyTorch 2.13.0a0, CUDA 13.3 forward-compat on kernel driver 580.178.04). Two NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, 128 GB) at `--tp 2 --parallel 16`, `--kv-dtype int8`, `--mtp-drafts 15 --mtp-confidence 0.70`, context 262144, NCCL over one RoCE HCA. Checkpoint `TensorFold/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP` at `2b170fa6309d5d1ee380b35636075fac7945f286`. "Before" is the same image and session with `TENSORFOLD_COPY_DRAFTS=0`.

**Exactness.** `tools/bench_concurrent.py ... --levels 1,4 --tokens 512 --alone --serial`, before and after: every concurrent reply equal to its solo run (alone 1/1 and 4/4 in all cells) and every solo run equal to `"draft": false` (serial 1/1 in all cells). Five one-stream requests sent twice, the second with `"draft": false`, token_sha equal in all five, before and after (table below).

**Decode speed**, `tools/bench_openai.py --reps 2 --temperatures 0`:

| prompt | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| fibonacci-raw | 91.9 tok/s | 92.9 tok/s |
| gpu-chat-no-think | 96.5 | 97.3 |

`tools/bench_concurrent.py`, aggregate tok/s: code 1 user 108.4 -> 103.7, 4 users 323.5 -> 320.7; chat 1 user 89.1 -> 87.9, 4 users 277.6 -> 273.2 (within this pair's run-to-run noise; those prompts repeat nothing).

The cells the change is for, one stream, greedy, 900-token replies, `tensorfold.decode_s` and `rounds` from the reply:

| cell | before | after | tokens per round | `"draft": false` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| copy a 3 kB passage verbatim | 127.8 | **337.1** | 6.3 -> 15.5 | 47.7 |
| fix typos in the passage | 129.5 | **321.7** | 6.0 -> 15.5 | 47.3 |

**Prompt speed**, `tools/prefill_cold.py` (2k to 64k cold prompts, 3 reps each), copy drafts off, on, and on again in the same session:

| prompt tokens | before: TTFT, prompt tok/s | after | after again |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|

Within the pair's noise at every length (the index is built after the prompt's first token is sampled: 0.12 s for 250k tokens on the host, 1 ms at 2k).

**Tests.** `tests/test_copy_drafts.py` (6, new; fails before the change with `ModuleNotFoundError` on the new module) and the full upstream suite inside the image on the CPU: this branch 4096 passed, 127 failed, 11 errors, 175 skipped; pristine `main` in the same container 4090 passed, 127 failed, 11 errors, 175 skipped, and the failure and error sets are identical (MLX-only tests and Triton kernel tests that cannot run on the CPU, such as `test_affine_rows.py` and `test_exact_sampling.py`). The six extra passes are `tests/test_copy_drafts.py`. The first push had one extra failure, `test_cuda_ignore_eos_engines.py::test_every_path_takes_stop_eos[True-False-flashnext]`: that test builds the engine without `__init__`, so the new attribute was missing; the reads are now `getattr` with a False default, as the surrounding code does for optional attributes.

**Not run.** Metal: no Mac here, and the change is CUDA-only (`families/qwen4_exp/cuda`). items.title: Flash Next on CUDA: image and video input on two ranks, concurrent and serial engines
items.body:
## What

Image and video input for Flash Next on CUDA on two ranks. Today the engine serves images on one GPU with `--parallel 2` or more and refuses `--vision` at `--tp 2`. Both ranks must feed identical hidden states into their halves of every layer; text does that by embedding the same ids, images only if both ranks hold the same features. So rank 0 runs the tower once per request and sends the result to rank 1 instead of rank 1 recomputing it:

- `engine.py`: the gate becomes "`--parallel 2` or more", on one GPU or two ranks. The tower loads on rank 0 only (`capacity_geometry` and `weight_transform` already took the rank, so rank 1 reserves 128 MiB and no weights); rank 1 prints that it attaches what rank 0 encodes. `--vision` joins the settings both ranks must share at startup (`_same_settings`).
- `multi.py: admit`: on two ranks, rank 0 encodes the request's images before the admission message, so an image the tower refuses fails on rank 0 alone and no message reaches rank 1. A request admitted again after waiting for memory keeps the features it already has.
- `multi_tp.py`: the admission message and its digest carry the image rows, the decode offset and the feature shape. After the plan agreed and both ranks' memory checks passed, `_share_vision` sends rank 0's bf16 feature rows and int32 rotary positions to rank 1 point to point (`comm.exchange`), inside the admission lockstep and before any round collective; both ranks reach it or neither does. `shape()` includes whether a slot holds image positions. An older leader's nine-field message still parses (no image).
- `multi_plan.py`: an image prompt reuses no kept prefix, keeps no prompt states and never takes the lone-stream graph slot, as on one GPU (`Shadow.images`).
- `image_rows.py`: `begin` attaches features another rank encoded; a prepared prompt still needs the tower.

Nothing changes in the prompt passes, the rotary kernel or the rounds: `image_rows.embed` and `attn_multi` read each rank's own copy of identical data. Video frames are image rows to the engine, so `video_url` parts work the same way when PyAV is installed. Image prompts on two ranks keep the one-GPU limits: no prefix reuse, no grammars or logprobs. Size: at most the request's visual-token budget x 2560 x 2 bytes (80 MB at 16,384 tokens) plus 12 bytes a prompt token, a few milliseconds on a RoCE link.

Rank 0 gives up the tower (0.84 GiB) and its 4 GiB encode workspace (`TENSORFOLD_VISION_WORKSPACE_MIB`) from stream-cache room: 53.4 GiB free for caches on rank 0 against 58.0 on rank 1 at `--parallel 16 --kv-dtype int8` on this pair, two streams at the full window.

I read #286: the Python engine is frozen and new work goes to the Zig engine. Flash Next is not on CUDA there yet, so this is offered as the reference and the measurements for when it is, like #468 (independent of it: this branch is `main` plus this one commit).

## Receipt

**Environment.** TensorFold `cb2ebf0` (v0.6.6 = `main`) plus this branch, inside `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3` (PyTorch 2.13.0a0, CUDA 13.3 forward-compat on kernel driver 580.178.04, transformers 5.18.0, PyAV 19.0.1 added for video). Two NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, 128 GB) at `--tp 2 --parallel 16 --vision`, `--kv-dtype int8`, `--mtp-drafts 15 --mtp-confidence 0.70`, context 262144, NCCL over one RoCE HCA. Checkpoint `TensorFold/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP` at `2b170fa6309d5d1ee380b35636075fac7945f286` (it carries the 27-layer vision tower). "Before" is the same image and host session started without `--vision` (main refuses the flag at `--tp 2`, so the before cells are text only).

**Correctness.** Greedy, thinking off, three probes with known answers:

| input | prompt tokens | reply |
|---|---:|---|
| drawn PNG, a red circle left and a blue square right: "which shapes, what colour" | 150 | "The image contains a red circle and a blue square." |
| 3840 x 2160 photo (a lake under clouds with two posts): "describe in one sentence" | 4,101 | "A serene, mirror-like lake reflects a soft, cloudy sky, with two weathered, rust-stained posts rising from the water's surface, their forms echoed perfectly below." |
| 4 s 320 x 240 video (a green frame turning red, a white square moving right): "what happens" | 373 | "The video starts with a green screen, which then changes to a red screen." |

**Exactness**, by `tensorfold.token_sha`, 160-token replies, four image prompts (the PNG and three questions on the photo):

| cell | result |
|---|---|
| drafted against the same request with `"draft": false` | 4 of 4 equal |
| four image requests sent together against each sent alone | 4 of 4 equal |
| a text request sent beside the four image requests against alone | equal |

Startup lines, rank 0 and rank 1:

```
[tensorfold] vision: image and video input, a 0.84 GiB tower with 4.00 GiB of workspace reserved; rank 1 receives each request's image features from this rank
[tensorfold] vision: image input on two ranks; this rank attaches the features rank 0 encodes
```

**Decode speed**, text, same host session, `--vision` off then on (`tools/bench_openai.py --reps 2 --temperatures 0`):

| prompt | `--vision` off | `--vision` on |
|---|---:|---:|
| fibonacci-raw | 92.4 tok/s | 89.3 tok/s |
| gpu-chat-no-think | 95.2 | 94.4 |

Frozen ruler (`bench_decode.py`, prose and structured, one stream, 3-run median):

| phase | `--vision` off | `--vision` on |
|---|---:|---:|
| prose (ends at EOS near 100 tokens) | 66.2 tok/s, TTFT 0.058 s | 65.2 tok/s, TTFT 0.057 s |
| structured (200 tokens) | 231.3 | 232.0 |

Within this pair's run-to-run band (the two fibonacci reps were 90.4 / 88.8 against 93.3 / 92.5 earlier in the day on the same image without `--vision`; the other three cells move under 1.5% either way). Text rounds take no vision code path: `attn_multi` sees no image positions and `image_rows.embed` finds no features.

Image requests, one stream: the PNG prompt decodes at 84 tok/s (160 tokens, prompt pass 0.09 s); the 4,101-token photo prompt passes in 3.2 s where 4,124 text tokens take 1.7 s (the tower's share about 1.5 s) and decodes at 70 tok/s. Four 4k-token image requests arriving together finish in 12-14 s each against 2-6 s alone: their prompt passes run one after another with `--decode-share 0`, as text prompts of that size do.

**Prompt speed**, `tools/prefill_cold.py` (2k to 64k cold text prompts, 3 reps), `--vision` off then on in the same session:

| prompt tokens | `--vision` off: TTFT, tok/s | `--vision` on: TTFT, tok/s |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,048 | 0.850 s, 2,411 | 0.853 s, 2,401 |
| 8,192 | 3.260 s, 2,513 | 3.259 s, 2,514 |
| 16,383 | 6.569 s, 2,494 | 6.503 s, 2,519 |
| 32,768 | 13.283 s, 2,467 | 13.240 s, 2,475 |
| 65,536 | 27.647 s, 2,371 | 27.517 s, 2,382 |

**Tests.** Inside the image on the CPU: `tests/test_flashnext_vision_two_ranks_host.py` (5 tests: the admission message and digest with and without images, both ranks share the tensors or neither does and they fall out of step; `begin` without a tower; image prompts off prefix reuse, prompt states and the graph slot). All five fail on `main` and pass here. The full suite in the same container: this branch 4095 passed / 127 failed / 11 errors / 175 skipped; pristine `cb2ebf0` 4090 / 127 / 11 / 175, the same 138 failing tests in both (Metal, MLX and network-bound tests on a Linux box without them). The vision, concurrent-decoder and two-rank planning tests (`test_vision_cuda.py`, `test_cuda_batch_admit.py`, `test_cuda_growing_caches.py`, `test_flashnext_round_plan.py`, `test_flash_next_tp_readiness_host.py`, `test_flashnext_absolute_grow_host.py`): 78 passed.

## Second commit: image prompts on the serial engine too

The `--parallel 2` gate on `--vision` goes. Its reason was the serial engine's CUDA graphs: a capture bakes in the rotary mode, and the captured graphs know no image positions. `prefill()` already took an image payload (it attaches the rows and refuses prefix resume for them); nothing called it. Now `Engine.forward` and `mtp_forward` run eagerly while the state holds image positions, text states keep their graphs; `generate()` encodes on rank 0 before the request is shared, `_share`/`_unpack` carry the image description (an older leader's message still parses), `follow()` receives the features on rank 1, `_decode` prefills an image prompt from its start and keeps no snapshot, `_serial` takes the payload for `"draft": false`. The two-rank transfer moved to `vision_ranks.py` (`describe`, `exchange`), shared by the concurrent decoder and the serial engine; both ranks validate the same description.

An image request on the serial engine decodes at the eager rate, text keeps the serial rate, and the image request's fresh prefill overwrites the engine's kept text states.

**Receipt, serial engine** (`--tp 2`, no `--parallel`, same checkpoint and settings as above; `--vision` off then on in the same host session):

| cell | `--vision` off | `--vision` on |
|---|---:|---:|

items.title: h3: MiniMax H3 video and audio generation on MLX (draft proposal, non-lane family)
items.body:
**Draft, as a proposal.** CONTRIBUTING asks for an issue before a new model family, and this one sits outside three of the rules every change must keep. I am opening it as a draft so the code and measurements are in one place for that conversation; close it if a video engine does not belong in TensorFold.

Thank you first: this is built on your family and kernel structure and on the tensor-unit practice in `kernels/qwen/dense/v1/lane_qmm.py`. The H3 code itself is adapted from mrbizarro's minimax-h3-mlx, and the int8 scheme follows antirez's h3.c. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` records both.

## What it is

MiniMax H3 is a joint video and audio diffusion model: a 33B transformer denoises one packed sequence of video, audio and text rows for N steps, then a ViT decodes video tiles. This adds `families/h3` and `kernels/minimax/h3/v1`:

- the transformer on the released bfloat16 checkpoint, the packed sequence, both sigma schedules and the joint denoise loop;
- adapters (runner layout and FastVideo `fastvideo-lora-v2`), merged in float32;
- int8 SwiGLU, QKV (with the q/k norm and rotation in the kernel) and attention-output kernels on the M5 tensor units;
- the video decoder, with the same int8 kernels by default;
- `docs/recipes/minimax-h3.md` with the measurements, and rows in the family, kernel and recipe tables.

It is two commits on 0.6.5 (`609ca419`), all in new files apart from the three table rows and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. The second adds first-frame image to video: the sampler holds the encoded keyframe rows at their noise level and steps only the generated rows.

## Where it does not fit the rules

1. **Lanes.** H3 does not decode tokens. The family exports no `load`, sets `LANES = False`, and `tensorfold serve` does not route it. Nothing in the lane engine, the server or any existing family is touched.
2. **Exact output.** There is no drafted-against-serial contract to keep. What I can state instead: the bfloat16 transformer equals minimax-h3-mlx's on a real first step (zero difference with the same input rounding), and the float32 video decode equals its decode on real latents.
3. **No precision traded for speed.** The int8 kernels trade precision, on purpose: activations are quantized per row at run time. They are opt-in flags on the tool for the transformer and a default with a float32 switch for the video decoder. A 20-step int8 render keeps the bfloat16 composition with different detail; with a 3-forward distilled adapter it lands on a different composition. If this is the "precision mode" conversation the guide mentions, I am glad to have it in an issue instead.

## It is not complete

- The text encoder (Qwen3-VL hidden states), the audio decoder and the MP4 writer are not ported. `tools/h3_generate_dev.py` borrows minimax-h3-mlx's, so the tool needs that repository on the path.
- No `tensorfold generate`, no checkpoint detection through `families.detect` (H3 is a diffusers layout with no root `config.json`), no resident engine.
- Text to video and a first frame only; no last frame or reference images. The first frame is encoded by minimax-h3-mlx's VAE encoder and vision tower, which are not ported either.

## Receipt

- **Environment.** TensorFold 0.6.5 + this commit, MLX 0.32.3, mlx-lm 0.32.0, Mac Studio M5 Ultra 256 GB, macOS 27.0.1. Checkpoint `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3`, `FL2VA` partition. Adapter: lightx2v MiniMax H3 Turbo v1.0 in runner layout.
- **Exactness.** `bench_concurrent.py` and `token_sha` do not apply. `tools/h3_generate_dev.py --parity`: video and audio max difference 0.0 against minimax-h3-mlx `7919020` on a real first step. Float32 video decode against its decode on real latents: max difference 0.0.
- **Speed**, 5 second 864x480 clip, 124 frames, 15,918 rows, same session:

  | | Forwards | Per forward | Denoise | Clip |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | bfloat16 | 20 | 13.9 s | 277 s | about 305 s |
  | int8 MLP, fused QKV, attention output; int8 video decoder | 20 | 9.3 s | 190 s | 210 s |
  | Turbo adapter, same int8 | 3 | 9.0 s | 27.6 s | about 50 s |

  Per block: MLP 81.0 to 41.4 ms, QKV with norm and rotation 46.1 to 22.5 ms, attention output 12.2 to 7.0 ms, attention 92.8 ms unchanged. Video decode 17.3 to 10.7 s at 47.1 dB. For scale on the same Mac: antirez's h3.c takes 7.85 s a step and 202 s for the 20-step clip, so per step this is still slower than h3.c.
- **Prompt speed.** Not applicable; no prefill, kernel, engine or server path of an existing family is changed.
- **Tests.** Host suite on the M5 Ultra: 4979 passed, 609 skipped, 14 failed. The same 14 fail on untouched 0.6.5 in this environment (`tests/control/test_cli.py` x4, `tests/control/test_pty.py` x1, `tests/test_glm5_prompt_kernels.py` x1, `tests/test_lane_fuse.py` x8); I installed `.[test]` without `tui`, and did not look into the lane-fuse and GLM ones. New: `tests/test_h3_*.py`, 33 tests, which skip the kernel cases where the tensor operations are unavailable. They are new tests for new code, so they did not exist to fail before.
- **What I did not run.** Any Mac other than an M5 Ultra: M1-M4 have no tensor units, where the family falls back to bfloat16, untested. Less than 256 GB of memory (the float32 adapter merge peaks at 103 GB). CUDA: the family has no CUDA engine. Picture quality beyond stills: motion and audio were not reviewed by eye or ear.

## What did not work

Recorded in the recipe page: an int8 flash-style attention kernel reaches parity with MLX attention and no better (95.5 against 95.8 ms), and block-sparse attention is not sparse enough on this model to pay.

## Notes for landing

- Files are under 400 lines each. The measurements live in the recipe page, as the other recipes do.
- The commit carries a tool co-author trailer; I know you remove those when you land a commit.
- MiniMax H3 is under the MiniMax H3 Community License, which limits territories. No weights are included.

A packaged install with a one-shot script and sample clips is at https://github.com/drowzeys/keys-Mac-TensorFold-MiniMax-H3-MLX.

items.title: perf(flash next cuda): copies from the context before MTP chains, windows growing to 64 rows (a file rewrite 3.7x, same reply)
items.body:
## What this changes

Flash Next on CUDA drafted only MTP chains, so a reply that repeats its prompt, such as an agent rewriting or quoting a file it just read, kept about 5 tokens a round. On one GPU, a round now first verifies a copied continuation when the context repeats eight or more tokens, as Qwen3.6 MoE does, and otherwise the MTP chain. A copy's window starts at 16 rows, doubles while copies land whole (up to 64) and halves after a break, as Nemotron's on M5 (0.6.3) and the 27B's do. A reply that rewrites the file in its prompt decodes **3.7x faster** (92.4 to 341.0 tok/s with one stream, 92.9 to 340.3 with `--parallel 5`) with the same reply: a drafted reply still equals `"draft": false`, which this change doesn't touch, and the replies below are byte-identical to 0.6.4's.

- **Why 16 rows wasn't the limit.** `MAX_DEPTH = 15` caps the MTP setting, not the verify window: a row's bits don't depend on the window's width. The new tests verify copies wider than 16 rows against serial decoding: eager and in CUDA graphs, one stream and three, a lone stream in the `--parallel` graph slot, bf16 and int8 caches, and under a grammar.
- **One stream.** `mtp_decode(prompt=...)` copies or chains (`copies.Copies`, on the 27B's `CopyIndex` and `next_copy_rows`). The engine's buffers and graphs take 64 rows, which its startup estimate already counted (`gdn_geometry`'s indexed rows), so the estimate is unchanged (87.57 GiB at 262,144 tokens). Startup captures 192 decode graphs instead of 21.
- **`--parallel N`.** Every stream keeps its chain's rows (depth + 1). Copies share the rest of a round's max(N x (depth + 1), 64) rows, oldest stream first (`copies.fit`), and each stream keeps its own window. The lone stream's graph slot takes 64 rows, and every slot's replay scratch holds 64 rows, since any slot may become the graph slot. The admission counts these (`indexed_stream_geometry(rows=, scratch=)`).
- **Order in a round.** A round's tokens join each stream's context before its next drafts, so `take` now runs before `_draft_all` (and before the graph slot's drafts). The streams that draft are still chosen by `last`, never by a client's stop, so two ranks draft the same streams.
- **Two ranks** keep MTP chains only, `--parallel` included.
- **Costs.**
  - Memory at `--parallel 5`, 262,144 tokens, int8 cache: the startup estimate goes from 84.91 to 86.81 GiB (its activation bound counts the round's 64 rows and the graph slot's 64). Measured, the memory left for caches goes from 25.3 to 24.6 GiB.
  - A stream with nothing to copy that shares rounds with a wide copy gets longer rounds: in the run below, a 512-token reply went from 12.8 s to 16.6 s, while all three requests together finished in 16.6 s instead of 35.6 s.
  - Plain decode: a copy now and then proposed inside generated code costs about 0.5% (below).

## Receipt

- **Environment:** TensorFold 0.6.4 (`6ea5ade`) and this branch (`93d080e`); PyTorch 2.13.0a0 (NGC 26.07), CUDA 13.3, Triton 3.7.1; one DGX Spark (GB10). Model: [`Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP`](https://huggingface.co/Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP) (`dadefa8`), served with `--context 262144 --kv-dtype int8 --ple-on-ssd --thinking`: at `--parallel 5`, runs alternated 0.6.4, branch, branch, 0.6.4; at `--parallel 1`, 0.6.4 then branch.
- **Exactness:**
  - `tools/bench_concurrent.py --alone --serial`, every cell on both trees: at `--levels 5` (`--parallel 5`), concurrent against alone 15/15 equal, alone against `"draft": false` 5/5 (sampled) and 1/1 (greedy); at `--levels 1` (`--parallel 1`), 3/3 and 1/1. None unequal, none failed.
  - Each copy-heavy request below sent twice, the second with `"draft": false`: `token_sha` equal in all nine pairs (this branch at `--parallel 5` and `--parallel 1`, and 0.6.4 at `--parallel 5`), and this branch's equal to 0.6.4's (`054057179d32`, `37197544ef24`, `9f34a97796e8`).
- **Decode speed**, `tools/bench_openai.py`, median tok/s:

  | Prompt | T | `--parallel 5` (0.6.4 / branch / branch / 0.6.4) | `--parallel 1` (0.6.4 / branch) |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | fibonacci | 1.0 | 73.5 / 72.6 / 73.1 / 72.9 | 72.8 / 56.1 (again: 73.5 / 73.1) |
  | chat | 1.0 | 59.3 / 58.2 / 58.8 / 58.9 | 59.1 / 45.2 (again: 59.4 / 59.1) |
  | fibonacci | 0 | 63.1 / 62.4 / 62.4 / 63.0 | 63.6 / 63.3 |

  In the branch's `--parallel 1` run, the sampled cells' second to fourth repetitions ran slow (fibonacci 72.9, 53.1, 54.3, 56.1, 64.9). Run again, fresh servers, 0.6.4 then the branch, they did not: fibonacci 73.6, 73.5, 71.2, 72.9, 86.0 against 73.1, 73.4, 71.3, 72.5, 81.5, with one copy proposed in all of those requests. `--parallel 1` never resizes its caches, so I read the slow repetitions as the machine's.

  `tools/bench_concurrent.py`, aggregate tok/s (0.6.4 / branch): 5 streams code 149.0 / 148.6 (T=1), 244.5 / 245.2 (T=0), chat 125.8 / 125.7, 225.5 / 225.0; 1 stream code 86.6 / 86.8, 67.5 / 67.5, chat 59.1 / 59.1, 62.0 / 61.9.

  Tokens a round for the rewrite: 5.30 -> 48.36. A round takes 57.0 ms -> 142.2 ms.

  The LRU reply runs after the other two on the same server. At `--parallel 5` its rounds take 61.3 ms on 0.6.4 (50.3 ms with one stream): when the rewrite grows the graph slot's caches, the slot's graphs go (`_state_changed`) and the next request captures the widths it uses again, and the branch's copies add a width or two. On fresh servers, the LRU reply three times each: 0.6.4 82.0, 85.7, 85.2; this branch 81.1, 85.0, 84.5 (3 copies proposed, 15 of their 48 rows kept); this branch with copies off 81.9, 85.4, 85.2.
- **Prompt speed**, `tools/prefill_cold.py`, `--parallel 5`, median TTFT in seconds (0.6.4 / branch / branch / 0.6.4):

  | Prompt | TTFT (s) |

  The change doesn't touch prompt processing. With `--ple-on-ssd` the n-gram rows come from the SSD, and the first branch run's short prompts met slow reads; the second matches 0.6.4 at every length.
- **Tests:**
  - On GB10 (Linux), with the `test` and `tui` extras and xgrammar, `python -m pytest -q tests` with `--continue-on-collection-errors` (`tests/cuda/test_build.py` and `tests/streaming/test_build.py` share a module name, so collection otherwise stops) and `--timeout 600`: this branch 5,243 passed, 268 skipped, 127 failed, 12 errors; 0.6.4 5,236 passed, 268 skipped, and the same 127 failures and 12 errors, none only on either tree. Those tests need MLX here (`No module named 'mlx'`).
  - The Flash Next and CUDA admission tests alone (`tests/cuda/test_flashnext_*.py`, `tests/test_flash*.py`, `tests/test_cuda_*.py`, `tests/cuda/test_logprobs.py`, `tests/cuda/test_qwen27_copy_index.py`, `tests/cuda/test_qwen27_grammar.py`): 1,820 passed, 25 skipped, none failed (0.6.4: 1,813 passed, 25 skipped).
  - On 0.6.4 without the change, the new and updated tests fail: `test_copies_from_the_context_give_serial_tokens`, `test_server_engine_streams_serial_tokens`, `test_streams_copy_from_their_context_within_a_rounds_rows_and_equal_each_alone` (bf16, int8), `test_copies_share_the_rows_chains_leave_oldest_first`, `test_grammar_streams_copy_within_a_rounds_rows_and_equal_serial`, `test_a_lone_stream_copies_in_its_graph_slot_and_equals_serial`, and the Flash Next cases of `test_parallel_window_that_cannot_fit_every_stream_is_refused_before_loading`, `test_flash_parallel_decoder_allocations_are_budgeted` and `test_quantized_caches_admit_longer_windows_on_the_same_budget` (they count the copy rows).
- **Not run, and why:**
  - Metal: the change is in the CUDA engine (`families/qwen4_exp/cuda/`), which Macs don't run.
  - Two ranks: copies stay off there, and I have one Spark.
  - Other GPUs: I have only the GB10.
  - The NVFP4 and EXL3 Flash Next checkpoints through the server: the change is in the drafting and the scheduler, not the weights path.

<details><summary>The copy-heavy requests</summary>

```python
import hashlib, json, urllib.request
BASE, code = "http://127.0.0.1:8888", "".join(open("src/tensorfold/cuda/streams.py").readlines()[:250])
TASKS = [
    ("rewrite", f"Here is a Python file:\n\n```python\n{code}```\n\nRename the class `PrefixCache` to `PromptCache` "

                   "statement in the class `PrefixCache`. Reply with an edit: first OLD, the class exactly as it is now "
                   "(verbatim), then NEW, the whole class with the comments added.", 3500),
    ("code", "Write a Python LRU cache class with comments.", 512),
]
def health(): return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(BASE + "/health").read())
def chat(content, n, draft=True):
    body = {"model": "m", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}], "max_tokens": n, "temperature": 0,
            "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}, **({} if draft else {"draft": False})}
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req).read())
```

items.title: perf(flash next cuda): batch SSD n-gram gathers across streams
items.body:
## What this changes

Batch Flash Next n-gram table gathers per layer when multiple windows are staged together. Each window keeps its own n-gram history and independently computed row IDs; their IDs are concatenated in segment order, gathered once, and copied into the existing staging buffers at offset zero. Single-window and EXL3 staging retain the original lookup/copy path and do not allocate a concatenated ID array.

This is the guarded version of the batching approach proposed by [optimisme in issue #368](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/368). It preserves model arithmetic, cache commits, event ordering, SSD reader settings and sampling. The runtime change is confined to `forward.stage`, with accompanying tests. The branch is directly on v0.6.5 (`609ca41`). The NVFP4 serving recipe requires the separate SSD reader support in [#334](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/334).

## Receipt

**Environment:** one DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, 128 GB unified memory, local NVMe); NVIDIA driver 580.178.04, CUDA 13.3, PyTorch 2.13.0a0 NVIDIA 26.07 and Triton 3.7.1. Checkpoint: `Mia-AiLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, revision `925d7be6c14c6c9442ef83e8f05b5a3c39304f69`.

Direct comparison of pinned [PR334](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/334) (`cbfda4f`) against that same source plus guarded batching, using Mia NVFP4 with SSD offload on one Spark. Four fresh servers ran **A–B–B–A**, with three identical 20-request panels per server. Each panel tested one/four active requests, greedy/sampled decoding and fixed code/chat controls, with exactly 128 input and 256 generated tokens. Both arms used a parallel-4 server, context 69,632, int8 cache, six MTP drafts, confidence 0.60 and ordinary upstream graphs.

Equal-cell geometric results, balanced across the two source orders:

| Phase | Decode metric | PR334 tok/s | + batching tok/s | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| First panel | One request | 37.84 | 37.84 | +0.02% |
| First panel | Four requests, aggregate | 104.54 | 107.39 | +2.73% |
| First panel | Four requests, actual individual streams | 27.95 | 28.84 | +3.15% |
| Repeated panels | One request | 39.22 | 39.31 | +0.25% |
| Repeated panels | Four requests, aggregate | 109.21 | 111.42 | +2.02% |
| Repeated panels | Four requests, actual individual streams | 29.35 | 30.01 | +2.27% |

Individual-stream rates are measured from each request's own post-first-token interval, not aggregate throughput divided by four. The one-request result is effectively flat. In repeated panels, four-request aggregate changes were +0.52% in AB and +3.55% in BA. Cell results were mixed: four-request sampled code was −1.34% balanced (AB −3.57%, BA +0.95%), and one-request sampled chat was −1.04%, negative in both orders. The first-panel four-request aggregate result was +5.74% in AB and −0.20% in BA. These are two process-pair observations, not confidence intervals or a universal speed claim.

Repeated panels still incurred 83–98 ordinary graph captures per panel. The reported serving times include those capture costs.

All 240 panel requests matched literal output token arrays and speculative work across sources/repetitions, with 61,440 output tokens and zero cached prompt tokens. The separate 24 correctness requests also matched. Independent source, health, guard, thermal and restoration checks passed for run `20261005-084856-decode-batch-guard-v2`. The sole runtime overlay was `forward.py`, SHA256 `e3c982d961c993ad91b5a08eb0cfdcd5dc3a491f1e8cbf669525ea2315ba3f65`.

20 CPU host tests pass, covering staged bytes across affine/BF16/NVFP4 reader faces, unequal/repeated windows, history and accepted-prefix commits, EXL3 offsets, capacity checks and copy/event ordering. Single-window and EXL3 tests explicitly reject ID concatenation. Command: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_flashnext_ssd_batch.py`.

The serving measurements cover the pinned NVFP4 checkpoint, short prompts, and one or four active requests. Affine/BF16/NVFP4 host fixtures verify staging correctness; the measured performance results apply to the NVFP4 workload above.

items.title: perf(flash next cuda): opt-in graphs for uniform and mixed four-stream targets
items.body:
## What this changes

Adds two experimental, default-off CUDA graph paths for Flash Next target verification with four concurrent text streams. `TF_FOUR_STREAM_TARGET_GRAPH=1` enables uniform windows; `TF_MIXED_ROW_TARGET_GRAPH=1` enables the mixed-window extension. The switches can be enabled together. Eligible rounds replay the existing model computation, with SSD staging, sampling, acceptance and commits outside the graph. Checkpoint precision and target arithmetic are unchanged.

The uniform family holds at most four graphs: per-stream windows of 2 or 7 rows, each with two recurrent-scratch parities. The mixed family holds four more: non-uniform windows totalling 13 or 18 actual rows, each with two parities. A table-driven Triton PLE convolution refreshes each row's stream, start and tail mapping so different layouts with the same total rows can reuse a graph without padding expert rows.

Admission requires TP1, six drafts, pending counts at most 7, distinct text states, and dense attention ending at or before 512 tokens within the attention budget. Unsupported shapes and modes retain their existing fallback. Pointer/integer tables and PLE tails refresh before replay; capture-time writes are restored, stale static buffers invalidate entries, and graph metadata does not retain replaced States.

The code is based on v0.6.5 (`609ca41`) and restores the tested `0a33ef0` graph tree. SSD reader support is separate in [#334](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/334); batching is separate in [#413](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/413). Neither PR303 nor PR304 is included in this code or the comparisons below.

## Receipt

**Environment:** one DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, 128 GB unified memory, local NVMe); NVIDIA driver 580.178.04, CUDA 13.3, PyTorch 2.13.0a0 NVIDIA 26.07, Triton 3.7.1. Four server slots, context 69,632, int8 KV, six MTP drafts at confidence 0.60, and n-gram SSD offload. Existing solo graphs remain enabled. NVFP4 uses `Mia-AiLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` revision `925d7be6c14c6c9442ef83e8f05b5a3c39304f69`; the MLX4 diagnostic uses `Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP` revision `dadefa8066e3be900a0d148d0f5a2f4eb1cf6534`.

**Original uniform path, isolated from batching:** PR334 versus PR334 plus the original graph change (`7c78d3e`), 256 output tokens per stream and five repetitions per cell. NVFP4 balances baseline/candidate and candidate/baseline runs; MLX4 is one ordered baseline/candidate diagnostic. Ratios use each process's median concurrent throughput, then geometrically balance the NVFP4 orders.

| Four-stream cell | NVFP4 graph on/off | MLX4 graph on/off |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Coding, greedy | +3.64% | +2.69% |
| Chat, greedy | +3.44% | +2.33% |
| Coding, sampled | −0.24% | −0.27% |
| Chat, sampled | +0.29% | −0.41% |
| Four-cell geometric mean | +1.77% | +1.07% |

These are within-checkpoint comparisons. Greedy cells improved; sampled cells were essentially flat. All repetitions, including first-use captures, are retained. Four initial captures accumulated about 0.68 seconds during each NVFP4 interval; counters confirmed 590 target replays in the NVFP4 interval and 565 in the MLX diagnostic. No capture time is subtracted or attributed to a specific throughput penalty.

**Serial validation with guarded batching held constant:** two further NVFP4 comparisons tested the additions one at a time. Each used four fresh processes in ABBA order and three 20-request panels per process: 240 timed requests plus 24 separate correctness requests, with the same 128-input/256-output, coding/chat, greedy/sampled, one/four-stream workload. Repeated panels are the geometric mean within each process, then balanced across the two processes per version.

| Addition | Fixed comparison control | Repeated single-stream decode | Repeated four-stream aggregate decode | Four-stream AB / BA |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original uniform graphs | PR334 + guarded batching | −0.17% | +0.66% | +1.21% / +0.12% |
| Mixed extension | Same control + original uniform graphs | −0.31% | +0.70% | +1.88% / −0.45% |

These incremental effects are smaller and workload-dependent. For the uniform path, repeated four-stream greedy chat was −2.43% overall, negative in both orders. For the mixed extension, first-panel four-stream throughput was −0.38% overall; repeated actual individual-stream throughput was +1.06%. Its repeated aggregate result reverses sign by order and does not establish a robust additional gain over batching. Ordinary target/MTP graph captures occurred in every repeated panel and are retained in the timings. The isolated and serial percentages must not be added or compounded into an overall speedup. There are two independent fresh processes per version, not 240 independent performance replicates.

**Prefill and TTFT, original uniform path only:** a separate ABBA test compared PR334 with PR334 plus `7c78d3e`, without batching or the mixed extension. Each code/chat prompt had two observations per version at 4,096 and 32,768 actual input tokens, one request at a time, greedy, four output tokens and zero cached-prefix tokens.

| Checkpoint | Prompt tokens | Prefill tok/s, baseline → graph | Client TTFT (s), baseline → graph |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| NVFP4 | 4,096 | 2,038 → 2,030 | 2.286 → 2.294 |
| NVFP4 | 32,768 | 1,855 → 1,845 | 17.966 → 18.069 |
| MLX4 | 4,096 | 3,732 → 3,715 | 1.522 → 1.528 |
| MLX4 | 32,768 | 2,833 → 2,824 | 11.994 → 12.029 |

These checkpoint/length averages changed by less than 0.6%, slightly slower. No prefill gain or statistical equivalence is claimed. Prefill rate is actual input tokens divided by the host-timed `tensorfold.prefill_s` diagnostic, not isolated GPU execution. Long single-request prompts use the eager fallback. All 64 warm/timed requests across the two checkpoints retained fresh-cache semantics and matching literal outputs and speculative work within each checkpoint. This receipt does not qualify the mixed extension's long-prompt performance.

**Correctness and tests:** 65 graph host tests passed at the restored tree. The original uniform path previously passed 31 CUDA cases without failures or skips. The mixed extension passed 12 actual-model byte-exact qualification cases in each of its two isolated runs, covering layouts at fixed total rows, both parities, State replacement/reorder/reset/resize, PLE tails, pointer refresh, 512/513 fallback, buffer invalidation and commits/continuations. Its standalone CUDA pytest entry point was collected but not run separately. The complete serial panels and separate 64-token correctness arrays matched literal outputs and speculative work across versions. Source/process identity, graph exposure, thermal/memory guards and service restoration were independently verified.

**Limits:** single-stream and sampled benefits are not established. Mixed graphs retain 31.55 MB of explicit tensors, excluding CUDA graph-pool allocations; total incremental graph memory was not isolated. No mixed-extension MLX4 timing, long-context graph path, other-GPU qualification, arbitrary stream-count, grammar, EXL3 or TP claim is made. Both opt-ins remain experimental and default off.

**Related work:** [#422](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/422) changes garbage collection before capture in `graphs.py`; it does not add these target-window graph families or touch their implementation files. [@jayleaton's #300](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/300) proposes generic lane interfaces and `RowGraphs`; this bounded path uses the existing Flash Next decoder. [@grearjake-star's #337](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/337) addresses lone-stream graph-slot retention for [#317](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/317). These four-stream opt-ins preserve the solo-slot policy; shared `multi.py` changes need merge review. The guarded batching control adapts optimisme's [issue #368](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/368) work and is not included in this graph diff.

items.title: feat(flash next cuda): support NVFP4 n-gram SSD offload
items.body:
## What this changes

Enables the tested Flash Next NVFP4 checkpoint to run on a single DGX Spark by offloading its n-gram tables to SSD. This supported path was previously unavailable in stock TensorFold, which rejects `--ple-on-ssd` for NVFP4 checkpoints. The existing opt-in reader is extended to read rows on demand without mapping the complete table as resident arrays.

- Supports packed NVFP4, scalar FP8 and BF16 rows, including indexed components in separate files, with the resident reader's scales and BF16 rounding.
- Bounds individual reads and closes file descriptors and read workers with the engine. Existing MLX affine tables remain supported.
- Changes storage and loading only: checkpoint weights, routed-expert kernels, target arithmetic and drafting policy stay unchanged.

Linux uses buffered `pread` with `POSIX_FADV_RANDOM`. Filesystem page-cache use remains possible; this is not direct I/O or a zero-page-cache claim.

The tested NVFP4 checkpoint is slower overall than the MLX4 checkpoint on this Spark. The exports use different precision recipes: the NVFP4 checkpoint retains higher-precision weights in some dense components and the output head, with different storage and kernel work. This PR adds a previously unsupported capability; it is not a speedup claim. Because stock TensorFold cannot run this NVFP4 SSD-offload configuration, there is no suitable like-for-like pre-change performance baseline for the new path.

## Receipt

**Environment:** v0.6.5 (`609ca419abecebdc5a059498a613680bd3aa847f`) and this SSD reader on one DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, 128 GB unified memory, local NVMe). NVIDIA driver 580.178.04, CUDA 13.3, PyTorch 2.13.0a0 NVIDIA 26.07 and Triton 3.7.1. Serving used four streams, context 69,632, int8 KV, six MTP drafts at confidence 0.60 and `--ple-on-ssd`.

**Checkpoints:** `Mia-AiLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` at `925d7be6c14c6c9442ef83e8f05b5a3c39304f69`; MLX compatibility/reference checkpoint `Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP` at `dadefa8066e3be900a0d148d0f5a2f4eb1cf6534`.

**Exactness:**

- Mia SSD-only smoke: six literal 64-token replies preserved fresh/resumed/serial equality across two prompts (token hashes `f670a977fd2c` and `88e6afad2e4f`). All four public concurrent/solo/serial cells passed. Startup confirmed SSD n-gram reads; the original service was restored healthy.
- MLX compatibility: all same-request token arrays matched across the four ABBA arms; 24 ordinary 64-token reply arrays preserved drafted/serial and fresh/resumed equality. All 16 public concurrent/solo/serial cells passed.

**Tests:** 177 host checks passed, with three MLX-dependent checks skipped in that environment and subsequently passed separately as CPU fixtures with MLX 0.32.0. All three isolated CUDA BF16/FP8/NVFP4 SSD loader layout cases passed without failures or skips. Fixtures cover resident/SSD equality, split-file components, invalid layouts, bounded and short reads, and cleanup.

**Limits:** the full NVFP4 2k–64k prefill matrix, other CUDA devices and full-model Apple Silicon GPU tests were not run. Mac checks were small CPU fixtures. Row-format support does not qualify every complete checkpoint using that format. Performance equivalence for the existing MLX path has not been established, and no quality advantage is claimed.

## Related work and attribution

Further performance work builds on this support in two separate PRs:

- [PR338: opt-in graphs for uniform and mixed four-stream targets](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/338) reduces target-launch overhead for eligible concurrent workloads. Its receipt reports the workload-dependent gains and limits.
- [PR413: guarded SSD n-gram batching](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/413) combines gathers across multiple windows, with measured multi-stream gains and essentially unchanged single-stream throughput.

Their implementation and performance receipts remain separate from this feature PR.

Native FP4 compute remains separate in [Jürgen Schmied's #211](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/211), including the MTP scale fix credited there to @SvangenStudios. No native kernel from that PR is included here. The contribution also stays separate from [`shards.N` admission (#330)](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/330), [EXL3 read-ahead (#252)](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/252), and [server file-descriptor limits (#294)](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/294). Main, open PRs and the [Landing next list](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/286) were checked before submission; #332 and #333 concern other families/shared geometry, not this row reader. Neither optimisation, nor PR303/PR304, is included in this SSD-support diff.

items.title: fix(cuda): tool_choice "none" keeps the tools in the prompt
items.body:
## What this changes

On the CUDA server, `tool_choice: "none"` rendered the prompt without the request's tools. The tools open the prompt (the chat templates list them in the system block), so an answer-only turn at the end of an agent's tool rounds had a different prefix from every earlier turn and could not resume from any kept prompt state: it prefilled the whole conversation again.

`"none"` now renders the tools the request lists, as vLLM does by default (`exclude_tools_when_tool_choice_none` is off). It still forbids a call: the reply is parsed with no tools, exactly as before. `"required"`, a named function and `"auto"` are untouched, as is the Mac server.

The existing `test_tool_choice_shapes_the_tools_offered` asserted the old rendering for `"none"`; it now asserts the new one.

## Receipt

- Environment: this change on v0.6.4 (`6ea5ade`), against stock v0.6.4, nothing else patched. One DGX Spark (GB10), NVIDIA PyTorch 26.07 container, `Vontra/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP`, `serve --parallel 4 --context 98304 --kv-dtype int8` for the tool runs and `--parallel 2` for the scenario. Unit tests: macOS, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.1 CPU.
- The case, three repetitions per build: a fresh agent conversation each time (system prompt, six tool calls with long results, about 57.4k tokens), greedy, thinking off, `max_tokens` 1. Request 1 is the conversation with `tool_choice: "auto"`; request 2 adds a user turn with `"none"`; request 3 is the control, the same request with `"auto"`.

  | build | request 1, cold (auto) | request 2 (none): cached tokens, seconds | request 3 (auto): cached tokens, seconds |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | stock v0.6.4 | 22.37 / 22.64 / 22.73 s | 0 of 57,085 / 57,047 / 57,001: 22.27 / 22.45 / 22.53 s | 57,477 / 57,439 / 57,393: 0.15-0.17 s |
  | this change | 22.74 / 22.80 / 22.89 s | 57,477 / 57,439 / 57,393 of 57,498 / 57,460 / 57,414: 0.17 / 0.16 / 0.18 s | 57,497 / 57,459 / 57,413: 0.11-0.12 s |

  Cold prefill is the same on both builds within run-to-run noise (request 1 differs by about 1 %), since nothing on that path changes.
- Exactness: `tools/bench_concurrent.py --levels 1,2,4 --tokens 128 --reps 2 --alone --serial`: concurrent against alone 56 of 56 equal, alone against `"draft": false` 30 of 30 equal, 0 failed (stock: the same counts). That tool does not send `tool_choice`, so I also sent a `"none"` request with tools three times (47, 120 and 53 completion tokens), each with `"draft": true` then `false`: the `token_sha` matched on all three. That check ran on an earlier build that also carried #263, #302 and two local CPU-side patches.
- Decode speed, `tools/bench_openai.py --tokens 64 --reps 5`, median tok/s, stock / this change / this change / stock: fibonacci greedy 69.8 / 69.2 / 69.0 / 68.9, fibonacci sampled 73.3 / 73.9 / 75.3 / 74.8, chat greedy 65.5 / 65.3 / 65.4 / 65.2, chat sampled 61.2 / 61.2 / 62.1 / 62.7.
- Prompt speed, `tools/prefill_cold.py`, cold TTFT in seconds at 2k / 8k / 16k / 32k / 64k tokens, stock / this change / this change / stock: 1.33 / 4.09 / 7.11 / 13.21 / 26.83, then 1.26 / 3.95 / 6.90 / 13.39 / 27.10, then 1.20 / 3.63 / 6.82 / 13.22 / 26.78, then 1.20 / 3.64 / 6.78 / 13.27 / 26.97. The first stock pass is the cold one.
- Tests run: `tests/test_cuda_tool_choice.py`, 10 passed. The changed assertion and the new `test_none_keeps_the_prompt_auto_renders_and_the_reply_stays_prose` fail on v0.6.4 and pass here. Full `tests/` on the Mac: 19 failed and 1 collection error (`tests/test_glm_exl3_bits.py`, no `triton`) with and without the change; 5,119 passed before and 5,120 after. I did not compare the 19 failures name by name.
- Not run: Metal (the Mac server is unchanged), two ranks, `--vision`, and the concurrent-against-solo hash with `"none"` requests.

## Checklist

- [x] Every token still goes through the lane rounds. No serial path, and nothing that needs drafts off.
- [x] Drafted output equals `"draft": false`, a resumed prompt equals a fresh one, and concurrent equals solo.
- [x] No precision traded for speed. If the bits change, the description says which sums change and why.
- [x] Prompt processing is no slower than the last release.
- [x] The description says which platforms I ran, Metal M1 to M5 and CUDA, and which I could not.
- [x] New tests fail before the change, pass after it, and skip cleanly without their dependency.

items.title: fix(flash next cuda): image prompts resume and keep prompt states, matched on their images' pixels
items.body:
**TL;DR:** with `--vision --parallel 2+`, Flash Next on CUDA never resumed a prompt that held an image, so one
screenshot in an agent's history made every later turn prefill the whole conversation again. Kept prompt states are
now matched on the prompt's ids with each image's rows replaced by a key of that image's pixels and grid. A follow-up
turn that resends the same images resumes past them, as a text turn does; a different image resumes only the text
before it. Replies are the same tokens as a fresh prefill.

## The problem

`MultiDecoder.admit` called `_slot_for(prompt, s.draft and s.vision is None)`, and `_keep_at` / `_point` returned
`None` for a stream with image positions. The guard is right as far as it goes: every image's rows are the same
placeholder id, so two prompts with different pictures in the same places would match on token ids. But it also
means an image request neither resumes nor keeps anything.

Agent clients (pi, Hermes, omp and others) keep tool-result screenshots in the history and resend it every step. From
the first image on, every step re-reads the whole conversation: at ~2,000 tok/s on a DGX Spark, a 140k-token session
spends ~70 s a step in prefill. Reported on the Flash Next Spark recipe
(MiaAI-Lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Single-DGX-Spark-TensorFold#5: 45 min of a 60-minute pi session was prefill) and for
GLM-5.3 on Macs (#220). The GLM recipe carries the same fix for GLM's CUDA path
(MiaAI-Lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks-TensorFold#11).

## The change

- `image_rows.key(prompt, vision)`: the prompt's ids with each image span's rows set to one negative int derived from
  `sha256(content_hash / grid)`. `content_hash` is the sha256 of the decoded RGB pixels the frontend already
  computes (`ImageInput.content_hash`, carried as `PreparedVisionPrompt.image_hashes`); the grid tells apart the same
  pixels resized differently. No token id is negative, so a text prompt never matches past a placeholder row.
- `MultiDecoder` matches, keeps and forks on that key instead of `s.prompt`: `_slot_for`, `_remember`, message-start
  stops, `_keep_at` and `_point`. The key lives in `fills[sid][4]`.
- A request whose images carry no hashes (spans, hashes and grids missing or inconsistent) gets `key = None` and keeps
  the old behaviour: no resume, no kept state.
- `prefill_begin(..., vision=)` attaches the prompt's image positions after `restore()` / `reset()` and **before**
  the resumed MTP tail is absorbed, so the tail rotates at the prompt's image positions as in a fresh prefill.
  `image_rows.begin` now only encodes and returns the payload. The serial `prefill` passes its `vision` the same way
  (it still refuses resume and keep points for images).

## Why a resumed state is exact

- Qwen's 3-D positions of a row depend only on the tokens and image grids before it (`image_positions`), so a prefix
  with the same ids and the same images has the same positions in any longer prompt. Text after the last image keeps
  its offset, so a kept point past an image rotates the same way in the next turn.
- `attach` installs the whole new prompt's positions; `embed` only writes image rows at or past `st.pos`, so features
  before the resume point are never used. Pooled QSA blocks that straddle the resume point are pooled once they
  complete, at their start row's position from the same table.
- Kept points are message starts and `entry_end`, never inside an image span (a span is only placeholder ids between
  `vision_start` and `vision_end`), so a resume never splits an image.
- Text rows before the first image sit at identity positions `(i, i, i)`, which give the same bits as plain rotary
  (`test_identity_image_positions_preserve_text_state_bits`). So an image prompt can resume from a text prompt's kept
  message start (a shared system prompt), and a text prompt from an image prompt's state before its first image.

## Not changed

- Every image is still encoded by the tower on each turn; only rows past the resume point are embedded. Encoding just
  the images past the resume point would save tower time but needs `QwenCudaVision.encode` and `validate_encoded` to
  accept a subset, so it is left for a follow-up.
- The serial engine (`--parallel 1`) has no image input, and GLM's CUDA path is untouched.
- Background replay already skips image streams (`Scheduler._yield`), so a replay never loses its images.

## Testing

- `tests/test_flashnext_image_keys.py` (CPU, 10): text ids unchanged, one negative key per image, keys follow pixels
  and grid, no key when images can't be told apart.
- `tests/cuda/test_flashnext_vision.py`, on the tiny model:
  - `test_a_follow_up_with_the_same_picture_resumes_like_a_fresh_prefill` (bf16 / int8 / int4 KV, image at rows 1,
    9 and 30): turn 2 resumes `len(turn 1) - 1` tokens, its tokens equal the serial reference, and its rounds, drafted
    and accepted counts equal the same request on a fresh decoder (the resumed MTP head drafts as a fresh one).
  - `test_a_resumed_picture_prompt_leaves_a_fresh_prefills_caches` (bf16 / int8): after a resumed turn the main and
    MTP KV rows are bit-identical to a fresh prefill's. It fails if the positions are attached after the MTP tail
    (the order before this change), which the token-level tests above don't catch.
  - `test_a_different_picture_or_text_resumes_only_the_text_before_it` (a different picture, the same pixels at
    another grid, the same ids as text): each resumes exactly the kept message start before the image and matches
    its reference.
  - `test_a_picture_follows_a_text_prompts_kept_message_start`: an image prompt resumes a text prompt's kept message
    start and matches its reference.
  - The existing tests still pass, including the ones that use payloads without hashes and assert nothing is kept.
- `test_flashnext_vision`, `test_flashnext_prompt_cache`, `test_flashnext_multi`, `test_flashnext_fill_arrivals` and
  `test_flashnext_fork_lanes` pass on a DGX Spark (GB10): 136 passed; the CPU files above plus `test_flashnext_fill_order`, `test_flashnext_prefix_fork`, `test_vision_server` and `test_vision_cuda`: 67 passed.

## Measured

One DGX Spark, `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` rev `7c4f1bc1`, `--parallel 2 --kv-dtype int8 --vision
--thinking` (thinking off in the requests), greedy, 64-token replies. A two-turn chat: a ~75k-token system prompt, a
user turn, the reply, a second user turn; the second request resends everything before it.

| Second turn | text only | a 640x400 PNG in the first user turn |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 75,610 cached, 0.54 s | **0 cached, 67.6 s** (whole prompt again) |
| with this change | 75,610 cached, 0.30 s | **75,857 cached, 0.37 s** |

Both builds are v0.6.2 plus local patches this checkpoint needs or that don't touch prompt caching: loading its
MXFP8/NVFP4 vision tower (as #249 does), copy drafts and prompt-piece rows, and #235/#239 (in the "with" build only).
The "with" build adds this commit, merged over those.

Both versions answered the second turn correctly from the picture. The same history with the picture swapped
(red/blue, then green/yellow, then red/blue again) resumed the 75,588 tokens before the picture each time and named
each picture's colours.

items.title: Support Qwen3.8 Flash Next NVFP4 vision on CUDA
items.body:
## Problem

TensorFold rejects the Mia-AiLab Qwen3.8 Flash Next checkpoint with `--vision`. After accepting its architecture aliases, the CUDA vision loader rejects scalar NVFP4 `weight_scale_2` tensors and would also reject the MXFP8 visual linears. Reported in #234.

## Change

- Accept the Qwen3.8 Flash Next model and Qwen3.5 vision configuration names used by this export.
- Validate ModelOpt visual tensor groups, dtypes, shapes, and scale metadata.
- Dequantize supported MXFP8 and NVFP4 vision linears to BF16 with TensorFold's existing format math.
- Account for expanded BF16 weights in vision capacity estimates and ignore quantization sidecars.
- Reject unexpected tensors and non-finite decoded weights; add focused regression tests.

## Validation

- 19 targeted vision/dequantization tests passed.
- Pinned Mia-AiLab revision `925d7be6c14c6c9442ef83e8f05b5a3c39304f69` passed header checks across all 37 safetensors shards. Real NVFP4 and MXFP8 matrices decoded to finite BF16 tensors.
- On a DGX Spark GB10, the candidate TensorFold image loaded the vision tower and returned a useful answer to a synthetic image through `/v1/chat/completions` (HTTP 200, 4.895 s). A text control remained `READY` before and after. Health stayed 200 and host MemAvailable remained 38.3 GiB, above the 20 GiB floor.
- Candidate settings: context 262144, temperature 0.1, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, min_p 0, int8 KV, drafts disabled, and `--parallel 2`. The previous text-only container remains available for rollback.

The end-to-end image check used a simple synthetic image and is a smoke test, not a broad visual-quality benchmark. Video input was not tested.

Fixes #234

items.title: Qwen3.8-27B CUDA: serve compressed-tensors checkpoints with channel FP8 scales
items.body:
## Summary

This PR lets the Qwen3.8-27B CUDA engine serve compressed-tensors NVFP4 checkpoints whose FP8 layers use channel scales, as many community fine-tunes do. It fixes three problems that stop such a checkpoint today. Tested with `orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-NVFP4` on one RTX 5090 (sm_120).

## Changes

1. **Channel and group FP8 scales** (`nvfp4_load.py`, `linear.py`, `format.py`)
   - The loader refused any FP8 projection with more than one scale: `FP8 with 10240 scales; the CUDA engine reads one scale a tensor`.
   - New `Fp8ChannelLinear`: runs the stored bytes on the existing per-tensor FP8 kernels with a unit scale, then multiplies each output column by its fp32 channel scale. Both steps act on one row at a time, so drafted, serial and concurrent rows keep equal bits. Trade-off: the output takes two bf16 roundings where a fused scale takes one. A kernel that takes a column-scale vector would remove this. I kept the change small instead.
   - Group scales `[N, K/G]` with `G` a multiple of 64 go to the existing `Fp8BlockLinear.from_rows`.
   - The 27B loader now also takes `fp8block` (`weight_scale_inv`) projections through `Fp8BlockLinear.from_checkpoint`.
   - `format.dequant("fp8", ...)` reads channel and group scales.
2. **Banded fragment order** (`linear.py`, `_fragment_order`)
   - An FP8 `lm_head` (248,320 x 5,120) needed two int64 index tensors of the full size and ran out of memory on a 32 GB card (`Tried to allocate 9.47 GiB`).
   - The gather now runs over bands of 64-output tiles. The output bytes are the same. A test compares it with the one-gather result.
3. **FP8 KV calibration scales** (`nvfp4_load.py`, `skipped`)
   - `self_attn.k_scale` / `v_scale` / `q_scale` made the load fail as unused tensors. The cache here is bf16, so the loader now skips them.
4. **Saved tokenizer truncation** (new `cuda/tokenizer_file.py`, used by `cuda/server.py` and `cuda/markers.py`)
   - This checkpoint ships a `tokenizer.json` with `truncation: {max_length: 2048}` left by its training run. `tokenizers` applies it on every `encode`, so the server cut every prompt to 2,048 tokens without an error.
   - The CUDA server now turns off saved truncation and padding. Prompts past the window are still refused by the server's own check.

## Tests

- `tests/test_nvfp4_format.py`: channel and group FP8 dequantization against torch float8.
- `tests/cuda/test_fp8_channel_linear.py`: decode and prompt paths against a dequantized reference, row independence (one row alone equals the same row in a 12-row call), `tiles()` and `out=`, banded fragment order equals one gather.
- `tests/test_tokenizer_file.py`: a saved truncation and padding block no longer cuts or pads.
- All pass on an RTX 5090, CUDA 12.8, torch 2.11.

## Served results (one RTX 5090, `--parallel 4`, `TENSORFOLD_MEMORY_RESERVE_GIB=2`)

- Loads in about 90 s. Window 34,815 tokens. 23.0 GiB at idle.
- Decode (512 tokens, greedy): code 189 tok/s, chat 81 tok/s.
- Needle at 10 / 50 / 90 % depth of a 29,754-token prompt: all correct.
- Tool calls with an array parameter: correct, thinking on and off.
- Four concurrent ~6.7k-token prompts with 2,048-token replies, then one 28.8k-token prompt: no errors, peak 29.5 GiB.

## Not in this PR

- The window on a 32 GB card is limited by the bf16 KV cache. `--kv-dtype int8` would help the 27B as it helps Flash Next.
- A follow-up turn on a ~29k-token conversation re-read the full prompt (9.6 s) where an identical resend took 0.23 s. I did not look into the cause.
- `--vision` on this checkpoint was not tried.
- The startup weight estimate does not count the expanded scales of the group-scale path (`Fp8BlockLinear`, 1/16 of the FP8 bytes). The channel path adds only one fp32 value per output.
